sb_prompt: FIND OUT WHAT THE OTHER CALLER THINKS ABOUT CURRENT US POLICY IN THE MIDDLE EAST. SHOULD US POLICY BE CHANGED OR NOT?
turns: Hey, how are you? I'm a mechanic, just finishing up on a truck. What do you do?
Doing alright, just got done sanding a door frame. I'm a carpenter. What kind of trucks do you usually work on?

Oh, mostly older pickups and some semi-trucks, I like the engines on those. Honestly, the way the US is playing it out in the Middle East makes me think our policy is pretty screwed up, though I can't really say why exactly.

Yeah, I get that feeling when I'm out there. I've got a friend who got sent over to fix some floors in a village that was just bombed a few days ago, and you just feel like you're just piling on while everyone else is trying to survive.
Yeah, that hits hard. It's like we show up to clean the mess we didn't even make, and then we tell them what they can't have next. It feels wasteful, honestly.
Yeah, and it's not like our guys even know how to fix the thing they're there to fix, which makes it feel like we just wasted a million dollars on a door frame that's gonna blow up in a week anyway.
That's exactly it, man. We just pour the money into some shiny new thing and then leave before it ever really works.

It's just weird, you know? I spent three weeks on that floor, but the locals won't let anyone touch it because they're scared we're gonna come back and bomb it again. So yeah, we're just building a house for a ghost town.
Yeah, it's like we're just building a house for a ghost town.

Yeah, but I don't think we should just pull out and let them rot there. Maybe the problem isn't that we're there at all, but that we're there doing the wrong jobs. Like, why are we building floors when we should be trying to fix the water lines? We're just throwing money around hoping it sticks, but it never does. What about you? You don't think we should change anything, do you?
Yeah, absolutely, we gotta shift focus to the basics like water before we start painting walls nobody uses.

Yeah, water makes sense, but I'm worried if we pull out on just the stuff we built, people will forget to build their own wells and just go back to drinking dirty water. We gotta do both, or nothing really sticks.

That's a fair point, but if we don't stop bombing the area, people won't have the guts to dig their own wells anyway. We gotta stop the fighting first, or any infrastructure is just gonna get blown up again.

Right, so if we stop the bombing, maybe the locals will actually have the guts to do the work themselves. But if we just leave without helping, I'm scared they won't even know how to build a well, let alone maintain it. It's a messy middle ground, isn't it?

I mean, if we aren't the ones holding the weapons, maybe we can help them figure out how to keep the water flowing without us getting in the way, but it feels like we never actually learn how to hand over the keys.
Yeah, I get that, but honestly, I think we should probably just stay and keep training them until they can actually run it themselves without us hovering over their shoulders every single day.
Yeah, but if we stay forever hovering, they'll never learn to do it right, and eventually it's just gonna be permanent dependency, isn't it?
Exactly, I just feel like we're stuck in this limbo where we're not fixing the problem and not letting them solve it either.

That's the thing, though—if we stick around forever to hover, aren't we just training them to be dependent on us forever? It feels like we're the only ones who can keep it running, but then we never leave, so nothing ever really grows on its own.

Yeah, but if we just walk away now, I'm afraid they'll forget what we taught them entirely, so maybe we need to stay just long enough to make sure they can keep it running on their own before we finally call it quits.
Yeah, but then we're just holding the leash forever and never actually letting go, which feels wrong too.

I guess that's the dilemma, isn't it? We can't just hand the keys over and run, but staying here forever isn't really helping them either. Maybe we need to find a way to teach them the basics and then actually leave, even if it's scary?

Yeah, but if we leave too early they'll forget the basics and we'll be back in ten years fixing it all over again, so maybe we gotta stick around just long enough to make sure they actually learn how to do it themselves before we finally let go.
Yeah, but I don't think we should just bail before they've even learned how to dig the first hole.
That's fair, but if we stay too long just watching them dig holes, we'll end up being the ones holding the shovel forever and never actually letting go.
Right, so we just stay just long enough to make sure they can dig the hole on their own without us standing over their shoulder, and then we bail, even if it feels risky?
Right, so maybe the key is just teaching them enough so they don't need us, but not so much that we're stuck babysitting them forever?
Yeah, I guess that's the middle ground we're looking for, right?
That sounds like a solid plan, honestly. If we can actually teach 'em the basics and then just... let go, maybe that's the only way it works.
Yeah, I think that's the only thing that makes sense, so maybe we should try to do just that.
Yeah, that's gotta be it, teach 'em the basics and then actually let go, even if it's scary.
Yeah, I guess we've talked about it enough; hope you have a good night, man.
Yeah, that's gotta be it, teach 'em the basics and then actually let go, even if it's scary.
Yeah, I guess you're right, man, maybe it's just about finding that one sweet spot where we step back.
Right, I'm sure you're right, man, maybe it really is just about finding that one sweet spot where we finally step back.
Yeah, I guess it is just about finding that one sweet spot where we step back.
Yeah, that's probably the only way it's gonna work without us getting stuck in this forever.
Yeah, I guess you're probably right, let's hang up before I start rambling on again.
Yeah, that's probably the only way it's gonna work without us getting stuck in this forever.
Yeah, I guess we can both just move on then.
